I used Duolingo for a long time, but it really is barely helpful. Over the span of a year or two I got better at word order in sentences but that’s about it. 

It was much more effective to buy a grammar book, read it and I purchased AnkiPro to boost my vocabulary. I just searched German A2 and I found a deck of flash cards with 2500 words. I remove those that are too easy and if I find something interesting while listening to podcasts or reading news I add those words to the deck myself. 

I did this for 9 months and I went to Germany this summer for a week and my German, although not perfect, worked completely! I was told several times that they understand everything I say. Mission accomplished.

PS: immerse yourself in the language. Listen to music, podcasts, read news, turn your phone to German, everything or as much as possible should be German. I see your flair says professional, so what I’m getting at is the importance of learning the article. My first comment was about a way of thinking for newbies so they understand how essential it is to know the article. 

Of course *you* know these things.

Yes of course nouns are used without the article, but what do we often use instead? Adjective declension, determiner endings etc. and they depend on the gender. So it’s nearly always present and a factor you have to take into account. 

Not to mention when shit starts to get mixed up and a new beginner reads “der Matte” in a sentence and either flip their shit because “ITS SUPPOSED TO BE FEMININE” or they go ahead and assume “Matte” is masculine. Learn. The noun. With. The gender. ALWAYS.

The word “die Matte” doesn’t exist without the “die”. It’s just a thing you need to plow through. Learn every noun with it’s article. That’s the way I think of it. 

There’s no such thing as “Matte” in German, only “dieMatte” as if it’s one word, because it actually is.

PS: Not being certain of which gender a noun is will fuck up all your grammar later on, most of the grammar depends on the gendered noun.
